_comment: Seed services and demo incidents. Two cohorts, both disclosed per Track 02 rules (bring-your-own dataset). 'core': 8 well-maintained repos verified 2026-08-16 to ship package-lock.json v3 with real commit history; 172 transitive deps shared by all eight. 'victim': repos found via GitHub code search for the malicious tarball names (chalk-5.6.1.tgz, debug-4.4.2.tgz) whose package-lock.json history actually pinned a compromised version — the real blast radius of the 2025-09-08 incident. Small projects, because that is who runs `npm install` inside a 95-minute window.

snapshots._comment: Lockfile snapshots per service: the last commit touching package-lock.json at or before each cutoff, plus dense hourly-resolution samples around each incident window so Q3 has lockfiles inside/before/after the window.

incidents.name: chalk / debug / ansi-styles compromise
incidents.note: PRIMARY DEMO. No umbrella advisory; MAL-2025-4696x..4698x per package. 806k dependents on debug alone. chalk@5.6.1 live 13:13:05Z -> next clean 5.6.2 at 14:47:54Z (95 min). Real victims in the 'victim' seed cohort.

incidents.name: TanStack worm (Mini Shai-Hulud)
incidents.note: SECOND DEMO / Q2 story. 42 packages, 84 versions from ONE advisory id, 5m39s publish window, advisory 4h52m later. Largest multi-package npm advisory in OSV. No seed resolved a bad version (0 real victims findable on GitHub).
